tickets.title: Record the current OBS baseline and public compatibility contracts
tickets.delivers: An operator can distinguish shipped behavior from planned changes and find the exact compatibility rules for settings and screenshots.
criteria: Record the source commit, lockfile identity, package version and current quality-gate results; retain historical study evidence unchanged.
Document exact names, opt-in/toolset boundaries, bounded recursive JSON limits, sensitive-field exclusions and each settings write's merge/replacement contract before feature implementation.
Record native-image result compatibility, existing metadata compatibility, retention ownership and supported screenshot save topologies before feature implementation.
Correct current transport/control/startup documentation and distinguish normal defaults from discovery configuration; link deferred findings to their existing destinations.
Retain TypeScript/Effect, schema-first descriptors, static registration and existing registry/quality gates; document pending gaps without describing them as fixed.
Record which existing resources can express the added locators; preserve unscoped resource contracts and explicitly explain inapplicable mappings rather than invent new resource APIs.
Record the supported Node runtime contract consistently with package metadata, documentation and the existing Node 22/24/26 acceptance matrix; identify any current mismatch explicitly.

tickets.title: Verify an installed package against controlled OBS
tickets.delivers: A fresh consumer runs a real MCP process and proves existing inspection, mutation/readback, audio, recording and screenshot behavior.
criteria: Extend the existing package-smoke seam to install a supplied tarball into a clean consumer and connect to a maintained controlled OBS endpoint.
Verify scene inspection and mutation/readback, audio state, recording start/stop and complete existing screenshot bytes against independently observed fixture state.
Record artifact identity, source/lock provenance, explicit configuration and timeouts in the report; clean up child processes and fixture resources.
Keep acceptance infrastructure outside historical benchmark snapshots; use a valid independently decodable image fixture.
Treat known pending feature gaps as explicit pending contracts, never passed tests; do not change production features to inflate the baseline.

tickets.title: Make package acceptance reject false success and uncertain outcomes
tickets.delivers: Acceptance fails when the server reports success without the expected OBS state, and reports faults without inventing a verdict.
criteria: Exercise OBS rejection, unavailable capabilities, timeouts and disconnects through installed MCP; record that each intended fault was actually injected and observed.
Distinguish confirmed state changes, failed changes, unknown outcomes and fixture-unimplemented requests; no unexercised fault or unsupported fixture case counts as acceptance success.
Handle valid contract-supported text/structured result forms; reject success-shaped responses when independently observed state disagrees.
Prove malformed image data is rejected by the acceptance oracle and timeout watchdogs leave a documented observation margin.
Preserve and verify existing no-replay behavior for uncertain mutations and batches; use focused protocol tests for applied-but-reply-lost cases where needed.

tickets.title: Detect protocol field omissions and documented restrictions
tickets.delivers: Maintainers can detect missing or stripped request fields rather than relying on request-name counts.
criteria: Compare a maintained pinned authoritative protocol snapshot outside historical research with actual exported descriptor request/response fields and declared public locator contracts, including representative outgoing requests; do not require workflow tools to mirror every raw protocol field.
Classify unknown drift, explicitly pending milestone gaps, intentional product restrictions and unavailable protocol capabilities separately; newly unexplained omissions fail the check.
Demonstrate detection of a missing locator and a schema-accepted field stripped before dispatch; restrictions require an explicit reason.
Correct descriptor versus request-name reporting and preserve batch-only Sleep; maintain existing registry/parity checks.
Feature slices retire their relevant pending entries only after forwarding and observable-state acceptance pass.

tickets.title: Verify existing subscriptions and screenshot retention
tickets.delivers: Users have an evidence-backed description of stateful subscriptions, stateless reads and latest-screenshot lifetime.
criteria: Reuse existing HTTP/resource seams to verify stateful subscribe/read/update notifications after OBS events and mutating tools.
Verify stateless HTTP does not advertise subscriptions and continues to provide resource reads.

Verify and document the recorded process/session ownership, bounds and lifetime of latest-screenshot metadata using the existing retention surface; align stale stateful-default and server-process wording with observed behavior.
Map each acceptance criterion of the existing stateful HTTP issue to evidence or a precisely described remaining gap; do not duplicate its implementation.
Record a reconciliation recommendation without modifying or closing the existing issue during ticket drafting/publication.
Preserve stdio subscription behavior and verify mutation-triggered notifications over actual stateful HTTP, alongside OBS-event notifications.

tickets.title: List scenes on the requested canvas
tickets.delivers: A client lists scenes for a supplied canvas UUID without silently falling back to another canvas.
criteria: Carry canvasUuid from the listed public schema through request dispatch under the recorded official contract; preserve existing unscoped resource behavior and document locator applicability.
Use installed MCP with multiple canvases and duplicate scene names to verify outgoing identity and returned scope independently.
Preserve unscoped/name-compatible behavior and capability/toolset policy; invalid or unsupported identity fails explicitly.
Update public documentation and retire the corresponding parity finding with passing field and behavior evidence.

tickets.title: Create an input in the requested canvas and scene
tickets.delivers: Name-based input creation targets the intended canvas even where scene names are duplicated.
criteria: Expose the official locator alternatives in the listed schema: a scene name with optional canvas UUID, or a scene UUID; reject canvas UUID with a scene UUID and other invalid combinations before dispatch.
Verify independently that installed MCP creates the input and scene item only in the intended fixture scene/canvas.
Preserve existing supported locators; test invalid combinations and unavailable capabilities according to the pinned request's rules.
Document the public contract and retire its field-parity gap; do not add unrelated canvas-management operations.

tickets.title: Select a program scene by UUID in tools and batches
tickets.delivers: Single calls and supported batches select the same intended program scene by stable UUID.
criteria: Accept and preserve sceneUuid in ordinary program-scene selection and corresponding batch items; preserve existing resource contracts and document locator applicability.
Verify UUID-only selection, name compatibility and request-specific invalid combinations against renamed or ambiguous fixture scenes.
Check both outgoing identity and actual selected scene; extend controlled batch behavior only as needed and reuse focused protocol tests.
Preserve batch order, capability policy, batch-only Sleep and truthful batch failure/no-replay behavior.
Update schemas/documentation and retire the matching parity finding.
Return truthful identity for UUID-only calls; do not fabricate a scene name or discard the supplied locator in single or batch results.

tickets.title: Read and update full-fidelity filter settings
tickets.delivers: Explicit settings access preserves permitted nested filter values while existing typed controls keep working.
criteria: Implement the recorded explicit settings read/write contract end to end, including unknown permitted keys, arrays, objects, null and finite primitives.
Verify packaged read/update/readback against nested plugin-style fixture state and independently observed changes.
Enforce documented size/depth bounds, opt-in policy and sensitive-field exclusions; show exclusions rather than imply an exact round trip.
Preserve typed convenience behavior and per-request merge/replacement semantics without unsafe read-modify-write.
Test malformed values, OBS rejection and missing capability through public boundaries; update contract documentation.
Apply recursive value limits and sensitive-field rules on both reads and writes, including nested arrays/objects; excluded data is explicitly marked rather than described as lossless.

Define explicit full-fidelity access for specific filter settings reads and writes; record whether list/default reads retain sanitized summaries and preserve their compatibility. Do not broaden every filter response implicitly.

tickets.title: Read and update full-fidelity output settings
tickets.delivers: Explicit output settings access preserves permitted kind-specific nested configuration.
criteria: Carry the recorded bounded settings contract through output read/write APIs without silently dropping permitted encoder/output values.
Verify nested read/update/readback and typed convenience compatibility from installed MCP against actual fixture state.
Enforce output-specific opt-in/sensitive-value exclusions and reject disallowed writes truthfully.
Document and verify the official write semantics, limits, unavailable capability and OBS failure behavior.
Reuse shared settings validation where appropriate without broadening input-settings or raw-request scope.
Apply recursive value limits and sensitive-field rules on both reads and writes, including nested arrays/objects; excluded data is explicitly marked rather than described as lossless.

tickets.title: Read and update full-fidelity transition settings
tickets.delivers: Users inspect the active transition's settings and apply supported nested updates.
criteria: Expose transitionSettings through the existing valid current-transition request; never introduce a nonexistent getter.
Verify packaged nested read/update/readback with arrays, unknown permitted keys and unrelated settings retained or replaced according to the official contract.
Keep typed convenience responses compatible and enforce the recorded limits, exclusions and explicit-access policy.
Test malformed input, unavailable capability and OBS rejection with independent state assertions.
Document write semantics and reuse shared settings validation without a universal raw dispatcher.
Apply recursive value limits and sensitive-field rules on both reads and writes, including nested arrays/objects; excluded data is explicitly marked rather than described as lossless.

tickets.title: Return bounded native MCP screenshot images
tickets.delivers: A screenshot tool returns complete native MCP image content with compatible metadata.
criteria: Return native image tool content with accurate MIME type and complete decodable bytes under the recorded compatibility contract.
Through installed MCP verify decoded content/dimensions where applicable, malformed or truncated OBS image responses, payload bounds, capture failures and capability/toolset restrictions.
Preserve latest-screenshot metadata correlation, ownership and bounded lifetime; reuse existing HTTP/resource tests and avoid a second retention surface.
Keep supported formats explicit; investigate expansion only against a demonstrated supported format and record the evidence/disposition.
Document the result contract; controlled images do not count as real-client visual acceptance.
Return native image bytes exactly matching the validated capture; an invalid capture must not replace latest-screenshot metadata.

tickets.title: Save screenshots with explicit OBS-host path semantics
tickets.delivers: Users know which host receives a saved screenshot and receive truthful results for supported topologies.
criteria: Implement the recorded local/shared/remote topology contract; never use an MCP-host path check as proof that remote OBS can write.
Retain filename/directory boundaries and document any explicit shared-filesystem assumption or unsupported topology.
Use a controlled endpoint with differing host path assumptions to verify outgoing destination and honest save success/error handling.
Preserve bounded retention and existing capture metadata behavior; document supported formats and limits.
Supply a reproducible save-topology check for subsequent real OBS acceptance without claiming the fixture proves a real file was written.
Cover traversal, missing configuration, a valid OBS-host destination absent on the MCP host, and OBS save rejection; distinguish acknowledgement from independently verified file existence.
Define whether saved:true denotes OBS completion acknowledgement or independently observed file existence; interpret path syntax and resolution only for the declared OBS-host topology.

tickets.title: Gate the complete installed workflow on supported Node versions
tickets.delivers: CI verifies the milestone's actual installed workflow under documented defaults and explicit opt-ins.
criteria: Extend the existing Node compatibility matrix and package-smoke workflow to run inspection, scene mutation/readback, audio, recording and screenshot baselines plus all completed selector, settings, native-image and fault scenarios against controlled OBS, including timeout/disconnect and lifecycle cleanup.
Exercise normal startup defaults separately from the explicit all-toolsets configuration; assert relevant behavior/capabilities rather than a minimum tool count.
Record source, lockfile, package identity, tarball digest and timeout configuration with each result.
Require existing quality gates and detect current dependency/runtime regressions; preserve historical baseline attribution.
Fail if any required workflow is pending, skipped as fixture-unimplemented or contradicted by observed state; keep real OBS outside deterministic CI.

tickets.title: Bind release preparation to one verified tarball
tickets.delivers: Release preparation produces one attributable candidate whose tested bytes are the bytes offered for publication.
criteria: Build/pack once for the candidate and install/test that exact artifact on the supported runtime matrix; retain its identity, version, source/lock provenance and digest.
Make the existing publication path consume the verified tarball rather than rebuild or publish the source directory.
Require acceptance evidence to match the candidate and fail on missing, wrong or changed artifacts; rehearse at a controlled publication boundary without publishing.
Account for every supported release entry point, including local release, so documented alternate paths cannot bypass the same candidate checks.
Keep existing authenticated publication policy and separate release preparation from maintainer authorization.

tickets.title: Verify registry attribution and safe publication retry
tickets.delivers: The release flow distinguishes a matching published artifact, a conflict and an unavailable registry.
criteria: Implement post-publication verification of exact package name/version and registry integrity against the candidate, instead of relying on the latest tag alone; exercise it at controlled boundaries in this ticket.
At controlled boundaries test absent version, matching existing bytes, conflicting bytes, lookup failure, propagation delay and interrupted publication.
Use bounded retry and explicit failure/resume results; never overwrite conflicting versions or move references to conceal failure.
Preserve candidate identity and acceptance evidence across a retry and document the operator recovery path.
Complete this implementation ticket without performing an actual npm publication.

tickets.title: Verify the release candidate in real OBS and an MCP client
tickets.delivers: Recorded evidence establishes that the exact candidate produces a consumable real OBS image and honors its claimed save topology.
criteria: Install the exact verified candidate, record its digest and OBS/client versions, and use an isolated controlled real OBS setup.
Capture an image through an actual supported MCP client and record evidence that its native image is consumable and corresponds to the intended scene.
Test each claimed save topology separately and record the destination host and actual saved-file evidence.
Run the approved visual check only; do not infer codec, device or live-streaming acceptance from it.
Keep this ticket open if access/evidence is missing; candidate changes invalidate evidence until the check is repeated.

tickets.title: Publish the authorized candidate and record release evidence
tickets.delivers: An explicitly authorized release is attributable to the accepted candidate and verified from the registry.
criteria: Obtain maintainer authorization for the identified candidate before any actual npm publication; ticket creation and plan approval are not that authorization.
Confirm quality, supported-runtime acceptance and real OBS/client evidence all identify the same unchanged candidate.
Publish through the prepared path and verify exact registry identity/integrity; record release evidence and any retry outcome.
Install the registry artifact into a fresh consumer and verify its identity and semantic controlled-OBS acceptance.
Leave release completion unresolved on conflict, missing evidence or unavailable authorization; preserve later milestone and investigation continuation.
